name: Fresh water
summary: Liquid water, the museum's one transparent liquid: the Salon's lily pond in the Nympheas oval (indoors, dyed black to a mirror), Chenghuai's garden pond (outdoors, a living green pond), and the grounds' long canal before the portico and the round basin on the walk east (outdoors, clear water over a dark bed). This record holds the water's own physics; what the pond has dissolved and grown in it is its history, and a dye is its working. Nature owns each body of water as an object (its level, waves and flow); Matter owns what light and sound do in it.

workings.note: Untreated water needs no working; the canal, the round basin and Chenghuai's pond are untreated.

constituents.role: the liquid; absorbs red light by its molecular vibrational overtones, so deep clear water is blue

constituents.material: coloured dissolved organic matter (humic and fulvic substances, tannins)

constituents.role: working water.dyed-black: the Salon pond's mirror

formation.how: The museum's water is mains or rain water held in built basins. Its colour is not a property of 'pond water' but the sum of the absorbers in it: the water molecule itself (a weak absorption rising steeply into the red), plus whatever the basin's life and surroundings add over time (algae, dissolved humic matter) or the keeper adds on purpose (dye). Each absorber has a measured spectrum; the total absorption is their sum, and light's path through the water (down to the bed and back) sets how much of the bed is seen.

absorptionIsAdditive.text: Total absorption is modelled as the sum of the pure-water term, a phytoplankton term that depends on chlorophyll a, a yellow-substance (dissolved organic matter) term and a detritus term, each a concentration times a specific coefficient.
absorptionIsAdditive.source: A. Morel, D. Antoine (2011) 'Pigment index retrieval in Case 1 waters', MERIS ATBD 2.9, PO-TN-MEL-GS-0005 issue 4 rev. 3, ACRI-ST for ESA, yellow-substance term (quoting A. Bricaud, A. Morel, L. Prieur (1981) 'Absorption by dissolved organic matter of the sea (yellow substance) in the UV and visible domains', Limnology and Oceanography 26:43-53), https://earth.esa.int/eogateway/documents/20142/37627/MERIS-ATBD-2-9.pdf

absorptionCoefficient.source: R.M. Pope, E.S. Fry (1997) 'Absorption spectrum (380-700 nm) of pure water. II. absorptionCoefficient.conditions: pure water, integrating cavity; tabulated in 1/cm, multiplied here by 100
absorptionCoefficient.note: Minimum near 418 nm (0.0044 /m); about 140 times larger at 700 nm. The spectrum is the truth: Matter integrates it against the eye's colour matching, never an RGB tint.

absorptionCoefficientCrossCheck.source: R.C. Smith, K.S. Baker (1981) 'Optical properties of the clearest natural waters (200-800 nm)', Applied Optics 20:177-184 ; tabulated by S. Prahl, Oregon Medical Laser Center, https://omlc.org/spectra/water/data/smith81.txt

internalTransmittance1m.derivation: exp(-a_w d) with d = 1 m and a_w from the Pope and Fry table
internalTransmittance1m.source: R.M. Pope, E.S. Fry (1997) 'Absorption spectrum (380-700 nm) of pure water. II. internalTransmittance1m.note: Pure water takes out almost 30 % of the red in a metre and almost nothing of the blue: the museum's shallow basins owe their colour to what is in them, not to the water.

wet.text: Water is the wetting film of every other substance: a film on a porous or rough surface darkens it by lowering the index step at the grains and trapping diffusely reflected light by total internal reflection.
wet.source: J. Lekner, M.C. Dorf (1988) 'Why some things are darker when wet', Applied Optics 27(7):1278-1280, https://doi.org/10.1364/AO.27.001278

stillSurface.text: Below the wind-wave threshold the surface carries only disorganised 'wrinkles' elongated along the wind, of micrometre amplitude; above it, regular waves grow.
stillSurface.source: A. Paquier, F. Moisy, M. Rabaud (2016) 'Viscosity effects in wind wave generation', Laboratoire FAST (CNRS, Universite Paris-Sud), arXiv:1611.01208, https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.01208

wrinkleSlope.derivation: rms height over streamwise correlation length: about 12 um / 200 mm at 3.2 m/s (see wrinkles)
wrinkleSlope.source: A. Paquier, F. Moisy, M. Rabaud (2016) 'Viscosity effects in wind wave generation', Laboratoire FAST (CNRS, Universite Paris-Sud), arXiv:1611.01208, https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.01208
wrinkleSlope.note: Slopes this small leave the surface a near-perfect mirror; the eye sees only faint streaking of sharp reflections.

windThreshold.note: The threshold depends on how the wind speed is defined (height, fetch); lab mean air speeds are not 10 m winds.

amplitudeLaw.text: Below the threshold, the rms height of the wrinkles scales as zeta_rms = alpha nu^-1/2 u*^3/2 with alpha = 1.9e-7 (SI), u* the friction velocity, approximately 0.05 times the mean air speed; water shows slightly smaller wrinkles than the law.
amplitudeLaw.source: A. Paquier, F. Moisy, M. Rabaud (2016) 'Viscosity effects in wind wave generation', Laboratoire FAST (CNRS, Universite Paris-Sud), arXiv:1611.01208, https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.01208

stock.note: A liquid has no stock: its body is the basin's volume, which Form draws and Nature fills (level by gravity, volume conserved).

physicalMaterial.note: Not walkable: the bodies carry no collision for the visitor (the old build's water had none, windows/Source/MuseeVision/Facade/MuseeLandscape.h). A contact with water is a splash, not a footfall.

photograph: Looking down near the edge you see the bed through the water; looking across, the far bank and the sky in reflection: the Fresnel curve, not a change of paint.
Reflections of verticals (trees, columns) are stretched into vertical streaks as soon as there is any ripple: the slope distribution, elongated along the wind.
On a still day a garden pond shows wind 'cat's-paws': dark patches where gusts roughen the surface and reflect less of the bright sky.
Clear water over a dark bed reads black and mirror-like; green water shows its colour mostly where the sun enters it and near the edge.
Dyed black water hides everything below a few centimetres: lily stems vanish at the surface, pads float on a mirror.
Floating pollen or dust leaves smooth, slick lanes where the ripples are damped.

Extrapolating Paquier et al.'s law to indoor air movement of about 0.2 m/s gives wrinkles of about 0.2 um, a perfect mirror; the law was measured only at 1 to 10 m/s.
